answers.answer: Refunds are allowed up to 30 days after the charge was created, counted from the charge's created_at and inclusive: a refund exactly 30 days (720 hours) after created_at is fine, one second later is refused with a Conflict on param `charge`.

Refuse the whole refund; never reduce it to fit. A refund may not be more than what is still refundable on the charge (the charge amount minus everything refunded so far, earlier partial refunds included). Raise a Conflict on param `amount` and change nothing. Refunding exactly the remaining amount is fine.

A refund's tax is the charge's tax times refund amount divided by charge amount, rounded half up to the whole cent, and never more than the tax not yet refunded on that charge. The refund that brings the charge to fully refunded takes all the tax that is still unrefunded, so the refunds' taxes always add up to exactly the charge's tax.

A refund of more than 10000 cents (strictly more than 100.00) must say who approved it, in a non-blank `approved_by` string; without one it is an InvalidRequest on param `approved_by`. Exactly 10000 needs no approval. The value is stored on the refund as `approved_by` (stripped), and is null when none was given. Smaller refunds may also carry one.
